scope: Cancel obsolete draft-media preview reads on new input, removed references, context changes, saving or editor exit while preserving drafts, unchanged players and independent explicit insertion/upload

before.sourceState: Final 13 cases, including corrected fixture versions, replayed in an isolated source copy against the verified revision-57 controller with N111 already applied. HTTP failures show obsolete connections still open after 3 seconds. Temporary copy removed.

fixtureSetup.reason: The first post-fix run reached save and exposed invalid fixture version strings one/two. Corrected to contract-valid 1/2, asserted editable session/version, then reran both final pre-fix and post-fix cases. This fixture failure is not a production defect.

application.skipReason: Native archive interoperability and registry agreement require VIENTO_TEST_ARCHIVE_BINARY; b.4.1 release native evidence retained.

observations: Initial manual browser steps were farther apart than the 15-second request deadline, so those first two close events only prove timeout recovery.

The second browser pass grouped input and save actions after 1.2-second debounce waits in one UI call. Both incomplete bodies closed in under three seconds, before the normal request deadline; the third preview completed.
browser.cancellationDurationOrigin: Elapsed from the proxy first-byte event to response close.

commands.before: Isolated verified pre-fix source copy: bundled Node v24.19.0 --test scripts/tests/media-preview-requests.test.mjs

testEnvironment: Actual editor and media controllers joined in an event-capable DOM. Two cases use the actual API client and real HTTP servers holding headers/body, checking response closure and a successful next request. Separate browser smoke uses the actual project service behind fault proxies, plus real UI editing, saving and reload.
limitations: Path/type changes and editor exit use controlled DOM/editor state; the browser pass specifically covers input/save cancellation.
The fault proxy delays already-parsed response bytes; client cancellation does not establish interruption of synchronous server parsing.
The first browser attempt reached the normal 15-second deadline; only the separately logged second attempt establishes active cancellation.
No native Tauri window, audio/video playback, Rust or native archive groups were rerun.

cleanup.automatedFixtures: HTTP servers closed; test callbacks handled both cancellation and late responses.
